_doc: WHAT THE CLIPBOARD HOLDS DECIDES WHAT PASTE DOES — D4 and D5,
ratified 2026-07-28: SWIFT IS CANON, Rust drops its internal-clipboard
fallback.
THE DIVERGENCE THIS FAMILY EXISTS TO CLOSE (LAYER_STRUCTURE.md 8.3):
D4  non-SVG text on the clipboard. Rust skipped the SVG branch and
pasted `tab.clipboard` — STALE INTERNAL ARTWORK the artist did not
copy — while silently discarding the text they did. Swift built a
Text element. Same gesture, two entirely different documents.
D5  an empty or unreadable clipboard. Rust pasted the internal buffer;
Swift no-opped.
Both are ruling R2 one level up: INVISIBLE STATE DECIDING WHAT THE ARTIST
GETS. Paste acts on what the clipboard HOLDS, and an empty clipboard
means there is nothing to paste.
THE `text` PARAM vs THE `svg` PARAM. `paste_layers.json` carries the
fragment MARKUP in `svg`, which presupposes the SVG branch was already
chosen. `text` carries the RAW CLIPBOARD PAYLOAD — the string the port
reads off the system clipboard, before any branch is chosen — so this
family is the only thing that can watch the DISPATCH. It is not a
parallel path: `text` routes through the same `paste_fragment_into` /
`pasteFragmentInto` body for an SVG payload, which is exactly what
`paste_clipboard_svg_payload_through_text_equals_the_svg_param` pins by
pointing at paste_layers.json's OWN golden file.
JSON null in `text` means UNREADABLE (the clipboard read itself
failed): Rust's `Option<String>` from the JS promise, Swift's nil from
`NSPasteboard.string(forType:)`. The empty string means READABLE BUT
EMPTY. They are different states and both must no-op.
GOLDENS WERE HAND-AUTHORED FROM THE ENCODING, NOT GENERATED FROM A PORT,
so the first run of this family was a real red in BOTH ports rather than
a port agreeing with itself. The Text element is Swift's canon verbatim:
Text(x: offset, y: offset + 16, content: text) with every other
parameter defaulted — sans-serif 16pt, normal/normal/none, NO FILL, no
stroke, unnamed, id-less, appended to the ACTIVE layer and selected.
WHAT THIS FAMILY CANNOT REACH, stated rather than implied: the WIRE from
the real system clipboard into that dispatch. Swift's is injectable and
is driven end-to-end by ClipboardTextPasteTests; Rust's still sits in a
`spawn_local` closure over an Rc<RefCell<AppState>> and a Dioxus Signal
and is NOT reachable from `cargo test --lib`. What IS reachable in Rust
is every line below the clipboard read, because the dispatch was lifted
into `paste_clipboard_text_into`.
BANKED, NOT DECIDED HERE: the canon Text element has fill = null (SVG's
implicit black), and whitespace-only text still becomes a Text element
because the guard tests byte-emptiness, not trimmed-emptiness. Both are
Swift's behaviour pinned as ruled, not invented.
name: paste_clipboard_family_setup_is_two_named_layers_background_and_foreground

_doc: D4, THE HEADLINE CASE. Plain text from another application. It becomes a
Text element holding that text. Before the ruling Rust produced the
setup document plus a COPY OF THE LAST IN-APP SELECTION here.
name: paste_clipboard_plain_text_becomes_a_text_element

_doc: Preserve mode degenerates to plain Paste for a text payload — there is
no layer name to preserve. Pinned by pointing at the SAME GOLDEN FILE as
the case above rather than by two goldens that could drift apart.
name: paste_clipboard_plain_text_preserving_layers_is_the_same_text_element

_doc: paste_in_place over text: no offset, so the element lands at x = 0 and
y = 16 (the baseline is offset + 16 in Swift's canon). Separates the two
halves of the offset, so a mutation that forces one cannot satisfy both.
name: paste_in_place_clipboard_plain_text_lands_at_the_origin

_doc: THE DISCRIMINATOR FOR THE SVG PREDICATE. Angle brackets are not enough:
the payload must start with <svg or <?xml. HTML copied from a browser
arrives looking like this and must become text, not a parse attempt.
name: paste_clipboard_markup_that_is_not_svg_is_still_text

_doc: The empty guard tests BYTE-emptiness, not trimmed-emptiness, so three
spaces are a paste and produce a Text element holding three spaces.
Swift's behaviour pinned as ruled; banked, not decided here.
name: paste_clipboard_whitespace_only_text_is_still_a_text_element

_doc: D5, HALF ONE. Readable but empty. Nothing on the clipboard means nothing
to paste — the document is untouched, in both ports. Rust used to append
the internal buffer here.
name: paste_clipboard_empty_text_is_a_noop

_doc: D5, HALF TWO. The clipboard READ ITSELF FAILED — JSON null, distinct
from the empty string above. Same answer: nothing to paste.
name: paste_clipboard_unreadable_is_a_noop

_doc: NO REGRESSION, AND IT IS PINNED BY FILE IDENTITY. The byte-identical SVG
payload that paste_layers.json feeds through the `svg` param is fed here
through `text`, and both point at ONE golden file. If the dispatch ever
stopped routing an SVG payload into the shared paste body — or routed it
into a second copy of that body — this case and its twin would have to
disagree, and they cannot, because there is only one file.
name: paste_clipboard_svg_payload_through_text_equals_the_svg_param

ops.text: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="16" y="16" width="16" height="16" fill="rgb(0,0,255)" stroke="none"/></svg>

_doc: The OTHER half of the SVG predicate — a payload that starts with the XML
declaration. Without this case a mutation deleting the <?xml arm would
go unseen. Same shared golden: the document must be identical.
name: paste_clipboard_xml_declaration_payload_takes_the_svg_branch

ops.text: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="16" y="16" width="16" height="16" fill="rgb(0,0,255)" stroke="none"/></svg>

_doc: A real clipboard payload often carries leading whitespace. The predicate
trims before testing the prefix, so this is still SVG — and the PARSER
must accept the untrimmed string, which is the part a prefix-only test
would not have caught. Same shared golden.
name: paste_clipboard_svg_with_leading_whitespace_takes_the_svg_branch

ops.text: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="16" y="16" width="16" height="16" fill="rgb(0,0,255)" stroke="none"/></svg>
